landmark_criteria.L1: Layout and engine channels: on two public scoreboards, controlled re-scoring moves at least one published method by >= 0.05 F1 or changes a top-10 rank. Status 12 Oct: met on one board (PC -0.07 / +0.07 by column order; authors' rule +0.2 for FCI; the agent's PC copy wrong on 36% of perfect-information problems).
landmark_criteria.L2: Name reliance across the field: >= 3 of >= 5 LLM-using systems lose >= 0.10 directed F1 from real to swapped names with shuffled columns, and a rho curve shows the dose response. Status: one system measured (Causal-Copilot 0.306 -> 0.142).
landmark_criteria.L3: Decision value: on >= 2 benchmarks with interventions, most methods are within 0.05 of 'nothing moves' while the identifiable ceiling is >= 0.15 above the best. Status: met on CausalArena semantic and formula (12 Oct).
landmark_criteria.L4: A constructive system: never below its data-only output on held-out data, bounded harm under swapped names, and decision-value precision at stated coverage >= 0.05 above the best reproduced method with calibration error <= 0.05, on >= 2 benchmarks. Status: format and verifier only.
landmark_criteria.L5: Theory that explains the measurements: the F1 = S x a identity and error budget, bounded harm, order dependence of conflict rules, the decision-value ceiling. Status: identity checked numerically; rest to write.
landmark_criteria.C1: Demand evidence: practitioners name decisions where provenance and abstention matter (interviews if any, teardown, public demand evidence labelled indirect).
landmark_criteria.C2: One vertical where order knowledge plus abstention measurably beats learned graphs (RCA probe).
landmark_criteria.C3: A regulatory or standards hook that rewards the ledger's guarantees (map, venue).

kill_criteria: if P9 is refuted (no agent loses >= 0.10 with swapped names), drop L2 as a headline and lead with L1 + L3
if P6 is refuted on a second benchmark (most methods clearly beat 'nothing moves'), L3 becomes a CausalArena-specific note
if no interviewee values provenance or abstention (P13 refuted), the product angle is shelved; the paper stands on L1-L3

bundles.title: Controlled scoreboard, CausalArena complete
parts: done 12 Oct: engine oracle (AUD-27), released vs shuffled re-score of PC/GES/FCI/LiNGAM/NOTEARS on semantic and formula (AUD-28), PC conflict-rule mechanism (AUD-28), sortability (AUD-29)

remaining: synthetic family; the D+I regime (GIES with the released targets, released vs shuffled); PC with maxP and with the order-free conservative rule on all families; a corrected leaderboard table (published, our released, our shuffled, rule used)
predictions: P1 GIES with targets gains under 0.01 from shuffling under the expectation rule and 0.01-0.04 under the authors' rule (refuted: |gain| > 0.05 expectation rule)
P2 PC with maxP: released and shuffled within 0.01 in all three families (refuted: > 0.03 in any)
gates: every published row we can run has released and shuffled numbers, both orientation rules, files paired
must_show: per-family layout gain by channel (authors' rule, conflict rule, engine copy)

bundles.title: Second scoreboard: do the layout and conflict channels exist elsewhere?
parts: pick two public benchmarks with published per-method numbers and released files (candidates from AU2: CausalBench (Wang et al.), bnlearn networks as used by LLM papers, CausalTime, CIPCaD); measure column order vs causal order, R2-sortability, and the released vs shuffled re-score of PC/GES/FCI
record which published numbers can be reproduced within their reported error
predictions: P3 at least one of the two releases lists columns in an order correlated with causal order (Kendall tau > 0.3) (refuted: both < 0.1)
P4 PC's conflict-rule effect (released vs shuffled q) appears wherever columns follow causal order (refuted: |delta q| < 0.03 there)
gates: reproduction of at least two published rows per benchmark within reported error before any re-score claim
must_show: per-benchmark table: order correlation, sortability, layout gain per method
risks: release formats differ; a benchmark may not publish per-method numbers we can reproduce

bundles.title: Engine forensics across the tools agents call
parts: extend the oracle check (AUD-27) to every engine an audited agent or library ships: causal-learn GES/CD-NOD/GIN with oracle scores where defined, pgmpy PC, dodiscover PC/FCI, gCastle PC settings, Causal-Copilot's other algorithm copies; Tetrad via py-tetrad if Java runs; pcalg only if R installs on Uzair's machine
determinism: same inputs, three runs, threads and processes; time-series engines (Tigramite PCMCI) with an oracle
file upstream-style bug reports as drafts (EXT-03) for Uzair to send
predictions: P5 at least one more widely used engine besides gCastle original/stable returns a wrong skeleton under a perfect oracle (refuted: all others 100%)
gates: every engine version pinned by wheel hash; oracle runs reproducible from one command
must_show: engine defect table: exact rate, order invariance, determinism, defect class

bundles.title: Decision-value scoreboard
parts: DV-1 (done 12 Oct on CausalArena, AUD-30) extended to: the synthetic family; Causal Chambers obs+int sample (53 regimes, physical ground truth); Sachs with its real interventions
DV-2: regret of choosing an intervention target to move a named outcome, vs random and vs the true graph
risk-coverage curves from bootstrap frequencies (no calibration yet); AID next to F1 for every method
the 'nothing moves' and 'everything downstream of inputs' baselines on every benchmark

usefulness threshold: the precision at stated coverage at which acting on the learned graph beats acting on 'nothing moves' or on a declared topology, measured as DV-2 regret, with the costs of wrong claims taken from AB-10's interviews
predictions: P6 on every benchmark, at most two of the reproduced methods beat the empty graph's committed-claim precision by more than 0.05 (refuted: four or more do)
P7 the true-CPDAG ceiling exceeds the best method by at least 0.15 on every benchmark (refuted: < 0.05 anywhere)
gates: baselines and ceilings computed on exactly the files each method finished; claims checked against truth; data-checked agreement reported only with the true DAG's own agreement as its ceiling

bundles.title: LIVE (small): agent probes, install and one-run cost per agent
bundles.llm_cost: one run per agent on one public scenario: Vashishtha et al. order elicitor, PyWhy-LLM pairwise, MATMCD, causaliq-knowledge, Causal-Copilot on a second model; cap $5 in total
parts: Claude installs each agent in the harness offline, runs it with the stub model, measures calls and tokens per run
Uzair runs one live call set per agent; the plan file caps tokens
predictions: P8 at least three of the five agents run end to end on a 20-40 variable CausalArena scenario (refuted: one or none)
gates: no key in any log; every call recorded; repo byte-identical
must_show: per-agent: installs, runs, calls, tokens, cost, wall time, failure points
risks: licences: Takayama, ILS-CSL, ArgCausalDisco have none; run for evaluation only, never redistribute wrappers

bundles.title: LIVE: field audit under names x layout controls
bundles.llm_cost: set from AB-05: about 3 arms x 10 dev scenarios x the agents that ran; Causal-Copilot $0.46/run measured; budget proposed in the AB-05 report before any spend
parts: arms: real / neutral / swapped names, all with shuffled columns; each agent's own data-only mode where it has one
scores: F1, S/c/q, DV-1, name-reliance (swapped minus real, per edge provenance where logged)
absorbs BND-12's second-model part for Causal-Copilot
predictions: P9 at least three agents lose >= 0.10 directed F1 from real to swapped names (refuted: none does)
P10 at least one agent scores below its own data-only output with real names on DV-1 (refuted: all at or above)
gates: thresholds hashed into the plan before the calls; dev split only; held-out reserved
must_show: where each agent's directions come from (provenance shares)

bundles.title: LIVE: knowledge elicitation (A3), what can a model supply?
bundles.llm_cost: about 900 short calls (DEC-02): tiers only, three phrasings, three name arms, 50 semantic + 50 formula scenarios
parts: prompt and thresholds hashed before the calls (O1-O5 of program v2)
post-cutoff and fictitious-name controls from AU2 (Srivastava graphs, Feng et al. design) on a subset
predictions: O1-O5 as pre-registered in program v2

bundles.title: Name-reliance benchmark (decoupled semantics, B2)
bundles.runner: Claude (free to build); agent runs inside AB-06's budget
parts: generator: CausalArena's released SCM sampler (or our own) with names taken from a second plausible system whose graph disagrees with the data on a set fraction rho of edges (rho = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
ArenaShuffle overlay (B1): server-side arms, declared regime, scored confidence matrices
scorer: AB-04's DV metrics plus per-edge provenance
predictions: P11 for name-reading agents, directed F1 falls monotonically in rho (Spearman <= -0.8) (refuted: no trend)
gates: the generator's own sortability and layout reported; columns always shuffled
risks: choosing 'plausible' second systems needs care; an LLM may be used to propose names, recorded as knowledge with hashes

bundles.title: Theory pack
parts: F1 = S x a identity and the three-term error budget (identifiability, finite sample, algorithm), with the per-scenario proof
bounded harm under I5: wrong knowledge can cost at most the directions it decided; tight example
order dependence of PC's collider conflict rules and why maxP removes it; the decision-value ceiling of the CPDAG
each statement checked numerically on CausalArena files
predictions: P12 every statement holds on all 500 public files to numerical precision (refuted: any counterexample, then restate)
gates: no statement beyond what AU3's references support

bundles.title: Practitioner interviews
parts: screener and interview guide (Claude); 5-8 interviews: IT operations / SRE, marketing science, real-world evidence, policy analytics
hypotheses: H1 they would use per-claim provenance and abstention; H2 they ask intervention questions, not graph questions; H3 a name/semantic dependence audit of their LLM tools is worth paying for
check with the course staff whether informal interviews need any human-subjects review before starting
predictions: P13 at least half of interviewees name a decision where 'which causes, how sure' matters more than the full graph (refuted: under a quarter)
gates: notes stored without personal data beyond role and sector

bundles.title: Competitive teardown
parts: hands-on with open tools (DoWhy + causal-learn, Tetrad, pgmpy, PyWhy-LLM, Causal-Copilot) on one public scenario: what each outputs, what it claims, whether it would pass the ledger verifier's checks, its decision-value score
vendor documentation for closed tools (causaLens, Causely, Datadog, Dynatrace): claimed guarantees and formats only, labelled as claims
predictions: P14 no tool records a per-direction source (refuted: any does)
gates: vendor claims never presented as measurements

bundles.title: Vertical probe: root-cause analysis
parts: RCAEval (or PetShop) incidents: learned-graph RCA vs BARO vs declared topology; add abstention and name-swapped service names
measure top-k accuracy, abstention value, and name dependence
predictions: P15 declared topology plus abstention beats learned-graph RCA on AC@3 by >= 0.1 (refuted: < 0.03)
